title: Sell Mineral Rights in Ralston, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Ralston, WY
metaDescription: Own minerals near Ralston in Park County's Bighorn Basin farm country? We confirm the deed history before making an offer.
heroLead: Ralston sits in the irrigated farmland northeast of Cody, part of the Bighorn Basin's older agricultural belt.
intro: This part of Park County is quiet farm country, not the site of major recent drilling, but it sits within the broader Bighorn Basin field system, and mineral interests here often connect back to older leases and units that have been producing steadily for decades. A Ralston-area mineral interest is more likely to be a legacy fraction than an active new lease, and we price it accordingly.

The community sits along the Bighorn River drainage, and much of the surrounding irrigated ground has stayed in the hands of the same ranching and farming families that settled it, with mineral rights following whatever the original patent or later deed language established.
Irrigation from the Shoshone Reclamation Project reaches into this part of the county too, and a lot of the same homestead-era title questions that apply around Powell apply here as well.

sections.heading: Legacy interests in a mature basin
paragraphs: Because the Bighorn Basin around Park County has been developed for so long, a lot of mineral ownership here is inherited fractional interest rather than a recently purchased position. If your interest ties to an older field nearby, that established history is generally an asset for pricing, not a drawback.

sections.heading: Confirming the severance
paragraphs: Farm ground around Ralston has often had minerals reserved separately at some point in its history. We pull Park County clerk records to confirm the severance and current ownership chain before we make an offer.

sections.heading: Next step
paragraphs: Send a division order, check stub, or legal description and we will trace your interest and put together a number.

faqs.question: There's no drilling happening near Ralston right now — is my interest worth anything?
faqs.answer: It can be, especially if it's tied to an established nearby field with a long production history. We check current and past activity for your tract.

faqs.question: How do I confirm I actually own separate mineral rights from the farmland?
faqs.answer: We check the deed history through Park County clerk records to confirm the severance.

faqs.question: What if I only have a very old lease document?
faqs.answer: Send it. Older leases still give us a legal description and starting point to trace current ownership.

faqs.question: Is my farmland interest similar to what you'd find near Powell?
faqs.answer: Often, yes — both areas sit within the Shoshone Reclamation Project's irrigated ground and share similar homestead-era title questions.

faqs.question: How does the Bighorn River factor into any of this?
faqs.answer: It doesn't change mineral ownership directly, but the irrigated ground along it has stayed in family hands for generations, which shapes how these interests typically got passed down.
